title: Wave Optics
seo_title: Wave Optics Class 12 Physics Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 10)
standard_text: Wave optics: wave front and Huygens's principle, proof of laws of reflection and refraction using Huygens's principle. Interference, Young's double slit experiment and expression for fringe width (no derivation, final expression only), coherent sources and sustained interference of light, diffraction due to a single slit, width of central maxima (qualitative treatment only).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Physics worksheets for NCERT Chapter 10 Wave Optics: wavefronts, Huygens' principle, Young's double-slit experiment, fringe width, single-slit diffraction and polarisation. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Bright: path difference nλ; dark: (n + ½)λ.
body_html:
How to think about it

A wavefront joins points vibrating in phase; Huygens' principle builds each new wavefront from secondary wavelets and explains reflection and refraction. Light from two coherent sources interferes: bright fringes where the path difference is nλ, dark where it is (n + ½)λ. In Young's experiment the fringe width is β = λD/d.

A single slit of width a gives a central bright band of width 2λD/a. Polarisation shows that light is transverse: a polaroid passes half of unpolarised light, Malus's law gives I = I₀ cos²θ, and light reflected at Brewster's angle (tan iB = n) is completely polarised.

Example

λ = 600 nm, D = 1 m, d = 1 mm. β?

λD/d

Answer: 0.6 mm

Example

Glass n = 1.5 in light: wavelength 600 nm becomes?

λ/n

Answer: 400 nm

Common mistakes

  • Thinking frequency changes in glass.
  • Using d in mm without converting.
  • Saying two bulbs are coherent.

faq.q: Why must the two sources in Young's experiment be coherent?
faq.a: Only coherent sources keep a constant phase difference, so the fringe pattern stays still.

faq.q: What does polarisation tell us about light?
faq.a: That light is a transverse wave.

c: every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets
light travels in straight lines only

items.q: What is diffraction?
c: the spreading of waves around an obstacle or through a gap
items.e: It is clearest when the gap is about the wavelength.
